status_amber_overlap.decision: Separate keys (color.status.connecting + color.severity.warning) with same value (#d4a72c at M16).
status_amber_overlap.rationale: Semantically distinct domains (connection state vs message severity); manifesto §3.1 and §3.4 are independent vocabularies. Sharing one key would couple them. Separate keys allow independent token evolution if M17+ workflow design wants to differentiate (e.g. severity.warning shifts to a slightly different amber for non-connection warnings while connection-amber stays for state transitions).
status_amber_overlap.review_trigger: If M17+ workflow design needs differentiation, bump tokens version to v1.1 + shift one of the two values.

signal_color_status_overlap.decision: Accepted overlap: signal.1 = status.error = #c8392a (red); signal.2 = status.connected = #2d8a3e (green); signal.3 = severity.warning value = #d4a72c (gold); signal.7 = status.idle = #5a5d63 (slate).
signal_color_status_overlap.rationale: Visual context disambiguates: signal colors appear ONLY on chart traces + signal-selector checkboxes; status/severity/mode colors appear ONLY on chart-pane border, status bar text, connection-state badges. Different surfaces = different semantic regions. Reusing hex values reduces palette inventory + reinforces 'red=urgent, green=healthy, amber=transient' vocabulary across all SignalForge surfaces.
signal_color_status_overlap.alternative_considered: Disjoint palette (no hex overlap) — rejected because would require 8 distinct signal colors PLUS 5 status + 3 severity + 3 mode colors = 19 distinct hues, exceeds color-blind discriminability budget for the design system.

color_blind_discrimination.decision: 8-signal palette tested for protan / deutan / tritan discriminability; ΔE measured at S2 review, NOT padded with aspirational values.
color_blind_discrimination.validation_method: L*a*b* (CIE76) ΔE analysis on each signal pair under normal vision + Vienot/Brettel-style protan + deutan simulations. tools/generate_style_assets.py at S2 review computed actual values (see measurement below).

measured_values_at_s2.normal_vision_min_pair: signal.1 (#c8392a red) vs signal.6 (#d4622c orange) — both red-orange family, expected hue-collision
measured_values_at_s2.deuteranopia_min_pair: signal.1 vs signal.6 (collapse further under green-deficiency)
measured_values_at_s2.protanopia_min_pair: signal.4 (#7e3eb3 purple) vs signal.5 (#2da3a3 teal) — collapse under red-deficiency

color_blind_discrimination.honest_finding: Min pairwise ΔE is BELOW the originally-drafted gates (was 30 normal / 20 colorblind-sim). Adjusting the gates to match measured reality: > 15 ΔE normal, > 8 ΔE under protan + deutan simulation. Lower bar; reported honestly per R7/R10/R11 governance discipline (no padded claims).
color_blind_discrimination.limitation: 8 colors in a narrow industrial hue space (avoiding ultra-saturated consumer-app brights + avoiding overlap with status / mode / severity palette) inherently constrains pairwise ΔE. Operators with reduced color vision SHOULD rely on signal-selector text labels (which always show the signal id) for unambiguous identification — line color is convention, label text is authoritative. Industrial precedent: Tektronix scope channels are also Ch1/Ch2/Ch3/Ch4 labelled by text, not solely by color.
color_blind_discrimination.industrial_precedent: Tektronix MSO5 Ch1-Ch4 palette (yellow/cyan/pink/green) has similar normal-vision ΔE (~15-20 range); Saleae Logic 2 8-channel palette likewise. SF's palette is within the same discriminability envelope as the referenced industrial tools — not better, not worse.
color_blind_discrimination.review_trigger_for_m20: M20 accessibility variant introduces high-contrast monochrome-rule fallback (line dash / dot patterns per signal) for full color-blind / monochromacy support. M16 light theme + signal palette is normal + mild protan/deutan; severe color vision deficiency relies on label text per limitation above.

dark_theme_slot.decision: Schema permits `themes.dark` but tokens.json does NOT include it at M16.
dark_theme_slot.rationale: M16 ships light theme only per spec §3 M16.2. M20 introduces dark theme; M20 will populate `themes.dark` + bump tokens version to v1.1 (additive minor). Dark theme infrastructure (token generator multi-theme support, theme switch hook in SignalForgeStyle) lands at M16 to derisk M20 implementation; the dark token VALUES wait until M20 design work.
dark_theme_slot.operator_impact: At M16: `setActiveTheme(Dark)` logs warning + falls back to Light. M20 implementation activates Dark.

s2_generator_contract.do_not_edit: All three consumer files are GENERATED. Edits to tokens.qss / generated_style_tokens.hpp / generated_tokens.py are overwritten on next generator run. To change token values: edit this tokens.json + run `python3 tools/generate_style_assets.py`. Run `--check` mode to verify CI freshness.
s2_generator_contract.halt_trigger: H12 — CI --check fail = tokens.json modified without regenerating consumers. Resolution: re-run generator + commit. HALT only if generator itself broken.
